title: Third Word Worship And Happiness Sin And Loss The Two Soldiers

questions.question: In the comparison, what were the two soldiers told to do at the beginning?
questions.answer: They were ordered to travel to a faraway city.

questions.question: What happened when they reached the split in the road?
questions.answer: They met a man who explained the difference between the two paths.

questions.question: What did the man say about the road on the right?
questions.answer: He said it usually brings benefit, peace of mind, and no real loss.

questions.question: What did he say about the road on the left?
questions.answer: He said it brings no true benefit and most of its travelers end up losing.

questions.question: How were the two roads alike?
questions.answer: They were equal in distance.

questions.question: What was one main difference between the left and right roads?
questions.answer: The left path had no order or authority, while the right path was under discipline.

questions.question: What did travelers on the left road not have to carry?
questions.answer: They did not carry supplies or weapons.

questions.question: What did travelers on the right road have to carry?
questions.answer: They had to carry food supplies and a strong weapon.

questions.question: Why might the left road seem easier at first?
questions.answer: It looked lighter and more comfortable because there was less to carry.

questions.question: Which soldier chose the right-hand road?
questions.answer: The fortunate soldier chose it.

questions.question: What burden did the fortunate soldier carry in a physical sense?
questions.answer: He carried a moderate load on his back.

questions.question: What heavier troubles was he saved from inside himself?
questions.answer: He was saved from deep fear and from needing to depend on people.

questions.question: Why did the other soldier choose the left-hand road?
questions.answer: He did not want to follow the army’s rules.

questions.question: What did the unlucky soldier gain right away by leaving the army?
questions.answer: He got rid of carrying the physical load.

questions.question: What did he suffer instead as he continued his journey?
questions.answer: He felt great fear, heavy inner stress, and dependence on others.

questions.question: How did he behave toward people and events on the road?
questions.answer: He begged from people and was frightened by everything around him.

questions.question: What happened when the unlucky soldier finally reached the city?
questions.answer: He was punished for rebellion and desertion.

questions.question: How did the obedient soldier travel emotionally and morally?
questions.answer: He traveled with peace, courage, and self-respect.

questions.question: What happened to the obedient soldier at the end?
questions.answer: He received an honorable reward for faithfully doing his duty.

questions.question: What is the main topic introduced in this passage before the story begins?
questions.answer: It explains that worship brings great gain and happiness, while sinful living brings serious loss and ruin.

questions.question: Who are the main characters in the story?
questions.answer: Two soldiers on a journey.

questions.question: Where were the soldiers headed?
questions.answer: They were going to a distant city.

questions.question: At the fork in the road, what information were they given about the right path?
questions.answer: Most people who take it benefit greatly and feel at peace.

questions.question: According to the man at the fork, what usually happens to people who take the left path?
questions.answer: Most of them end up losing.

questions.question: What false attraction did the left path have?
questions.answer: It seemed easier because there was no load and no authority over the traveler.

questions.question: Why was the right path harder on the outside?
questions.answer: It required the travelers to carry provisions and a weapon and to stay under discipline.

questions.question: What does the weapon on the right path suggest about that road?
questions.answer: It suggests that the traveler is prepared and protected against danger.

questions.question: How did the fortunate soldier respond to the advice?
questions.answer: He accepted the disciplined path and carried the required load.

questions.question: What was the result of his choice for his heart and spirit?
questions.answer: He felt inward relief and freedom from great fears and humiliations.

questions.question: How did the other soldier respond to the same advice?
questions.answer: He rejected the army’s order and chose the uncontrolled path.

questions.question: What happened to him even though he avoided the smaller burden?
questions.answer: He fell into much greater emotional and spiritual burdens.

questions.question: What details show that the second soldier lost his dignity?
questions.answer: He had to ask others for help and shook in fear before things around him.

questions.question: How does the ending of each soldier show a clear contrast?
questions.answer: One is honored and rewarded, while the other is punished in disgrace.

questions.question: Why is the ease of the left path called deceptive?
questions.answer: It looked comfortable at first, but it led to fear, neediness, and punishment.

questions.question: What value is praised through the soldier who obeyed?
questions.answer: Faithful obedience to rightful command.

questions.question: What warning is given through the soldier who deserted?
questions.answer: Refusing guidance and discipline can lead to loss in both the journey and the final outcome.

questions.question: What two opposite ways of life are compared in the opening sentence of the passage?
questions.answer: Worship is compared with vice and careless sinful living.

questions.question: Why is the story called a comparison?
questions.answer: It uses a simple journey story to teach a deeper lesson about life choices.

questions.question: What job or role did both travelers have?
questions.answer: They were soldiers.

questions.question: What does meeting a guide at the fork in the road add to the story?
questions.answer: It shows that they were clearly warned and informed before choosing.

questions.question: What percentage of travelers on the right road were said to gain profit and peace?
questions.answer: Nine out of ten.

questions.question: What percentage on the left road were said to suffer loss?
questions.answer: Nine out of ten.

questions.question: Why is it important that both roads are equal in distance?
questions.answer: It shows the better path is not longer, only different in character and result.

questions.question: What two things were required on the right road?
questions.answer: A supply bag and a rifle.

questions.question: What decision did the blessed soldier make?
questions.answer: He accepted the disciplined road despite its load.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the effect of that load on his inner life?
questions.answer: The outer weight was small, but it saved him from much heavier inner pain.

questions.question: What wrong idea did the other soldier follow?
questions.answer: He thought avoiding rules would make life easier.

questions.question: What happened to his heart after that choice?
questions.answer: It became burdened with heavy pressure and debt-like need.

questions.question: What happened to his spirit?
questions.answer: It was overwhelmed by many fears.

questions.question: What does his begging from everyone show?
questions.answer: It shows weakness, dependence, and loss of freedom.

questions.question: What does his fear of every object and event show about life without proper guidance?
questions.answer: It shows that such a life can fill a person with anxiety and insecurity.

questions.question: Why was he punished at the end?
questions.answer: He had abandoned his duty and rebelled.

questions.question: Why was the other soldier rewarded?
questions.answer: He stayed loyal, kept his equipment, and fulfilled his responsibility.

questions.question: In this story, what choice were the two soldiers forced to make?
questions.answer: They had to choose between a disciplined road and an undisciplined road.

questions.question: What advice did the man at the fork give before they chose?
questions.answer: He explained which path usually brought benefit and which one usually led to loss.

questions.question: What made the right-hand road seem more difficult at first glance?
questions.answer: It required carrying gear and living under command.

questions.question: What made the left-hand road seem attractive at first glance?
questions.answer: It offered freedom from rules, baggage, and weapons.

questions.question: Which soldier thought beyond the outside appearance of the road?
questions.answer: The fortunate soldier did.

questions.question: Which soldier focused more on short-term comfort?
questions.answer: The unfortunate soldier did.

questions.question: What happened to the fortunate soldier’s emotional state during the journey?
questions.answer: He stayed calm, unafraid, and inwardly at ease.

questions.question: What happened to the unfortunate soldier’s emotional state during the journey?
questions.answer: He became fearful, burdened, and restless.

questions.question: How does the story show that freedom without guidance is not true freedom?
questions.answer: The soldier who escaped discipline became dependent on others and afraid of everything.

questions.question: How does the story show that discipline can actually protect a person?
questions.answer: The obedient soldier’s equipment and order helped him travel safely and honorably.

questions.question: What contrast is made between physical weight and inner weight?
questions.answer: A small outer burden can remove a much bigger burden from the heart.

questions.question: Which soldier was more independent in the best sense?
questions.answer: The obedient soldier was, because he did not need to beg or fear others.

questions.question: What mistake led the second soldier to ruin?
questions.answer: He refused to follow rightful order.

questions.question: What final result matched his bad choice?
questions.answer: He was treated as a rebel and deserter.

questions.question: What final result matched the first soldier’s good choice?
questions.answer: He was honored with a fitting reward.

questions.question: What does the passage say a person will understand by listening to this comparison?
questions.answer: He will understand the great gain in worship and the great harm in sinful living.

questions.question: How many soldiers are in the story, and what do they share at the start?
questions.answer: There are two soldiers, and both begin with the same mission and travel together.

questions.question: What important place did they reach on their journey?
questions.answer: They came to a place where the road split in two.

questions.question: What kind of information did the man at the fork provide?
questions.answer: He gave practical advice about the results and conditions of each road.

questions.question: What benefit was linked with the right road besides profit?
questions.answer: Peace of mind.

questions.question: What lack was linked with the left road besides loss?
questions.answer: It offered no real advantage.

questions.question: Why is carrying a weapon important in the story?
questions.answer: It shows the traveler has protection and strength against dangers.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the weapon defeating enemies suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests the traveler on the right path is equipped to face threats successfully.

questions.question: What happened after the soldiers heard the explanation?
questions.answer: Each soldier made a different choice.

questions.question: How is the first soldier described by the passage?
questions.answer: He is described as fortunate.

questions.question: How is the second soldier described by the passage?
questions.answer: He is described as unlucky.

questions.question: What did the first soldier lose outwardly?
questions.answer: He had to accept carrying a noticeable load.

questions.question: What did he gain inwardly?
questions.answer: He gained peace and freedom from heavy fear and dependence.

questions.question: What did the second soldier avoid outwardly?
questions.answer: He avoided carrying the load.

questions.question: What did he suffer inwardly?
questions.answer: He suffered anxiety, humiliation, and inner heaviness.

questions.question: What actions showed his weakness during the trip?
questions.answer: He begged from people and trembled at things around him.

questions.question: What does the punishment at the end tell us about his choice?
questions.answer: It shows that his choice was not just unwise but also a betrayal of duty.

questions.question: What does the reward at the end tell us about the first soldier?
questions.answer: It shows his loyalty and obedience were valued and accepted.

questions.question: What Qur’anic command is placed near the beginning of this passage?
questions.answer: It is a call for people to worship.

questions.question: What two outcomes are connected to worship in the introduction?
questions.answer: Great profit and happiness.

questions.question: What two outcomes are connected to vice and dissipation in the introduction?
questions.answer: Great loss and ruin.

questions.question: What order had the two soldiers received?
questions.answer: They had been commanded to go to a far city.

questions.question: What did the man at the fork say about the right-hand road’s results for most people?
questions.answer: Most people who choose it gain much and feel secure inside.

questions.question: What did he say about the left-hand road’s results for most people?
questions.answer: Most people who choose it lose out.

questions.question: What was missing on the left-hand road that existed on the right?
questions.answer: Authority, rules, supplies, and weapons were missing.

questions.question: Why can lack of authority become dangerous in the story?
questions.answer: Because without order, a person is left weak and unprotected.

questions.question: What choice did the soldier who was blessed make?
questions.answer: He took the right road and accepted its responsibilities.

questions.question: What surprising result came from carrying the load?
questions.answer: A small physical burden kept him from huge emotional and spiritual burdens.

questions.question: What choice did the other soldier make?
questions.answer: He abandoned the army’s order and took the left road.

questions.question: What was his reason for leaving?
questions.answer: He did not want to submit to discipline.

questions.question: What did his path do to his relationship with others?
questions.answer: It made him needy toward people and lowered him to begging.

questions.question: What did his path do to his sense of safety?
questions.answer: It made him frightened by nearly everything.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the two soldiers’ hearts?
questions.answer: One had a heart at ease, while the other had a heart weighed down.

questions.question: How does the passage compare their consciences or inner condition?
questions.answer: One traveled with inner comfort, while the other suffered inwardly.

questions.question: What happened when the obedient soldier reached the city?
questions.answer: He was given an honorable reward.

questions.question: What happened when the deserter reached the city?
questions.answer: He was punished for rebellion and leaving his duty.
